quickAnswer: In Maynard, 31.7% of homes date from 1939 or earlier (4th-highest of 50 towns) and 63.9% of occupied homes heat with utility gas (ACS 2022). Oil is the minority fuel here, at 20.8%.
body: ## Fourth-highest share of pre-1940 homes, and mostly on gas

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), Maynard has 4,653 housing units, and 1,474 of them (31.7%) date from 1939 or earlier. That is the 4th-highest share among the 50 towns we serve, where the middle town sits at 16.6%. Altogether 3,300 homes (70.9%) predate 1980, 6th-highest, and the median home dates to 1963, the 6th oldest. Only 206 homes (4.4%) have been built since 2010.

Utility gas heats 2,822 occupied homes (63.9%), 7th-highest of the 50. Fuel oil heats 917 (20.8%), 43rd of 50, and the middle town is at 36.5%. Electricity heats 447 homes (10.1%) and bottled or tank (LP) gas 179 (4.1%). With gas the leading fuel, a replacement often starts with a gas boiler or furnace, and oil-to-gas conversion is less likely to be the main question than in towns where oil leads.
## What the mills left behind

Maynard grew around the Assabet River and the Assabet Woolen Mill. Amory Maynard and William Knight built a carpet mill in 1846 and 1847, the mill produced wool fabrics until 1950, and the town was incorporated in 1871 with 1,820 residents. The American Woolen Company bought the mill in 1899 and expanded the complex from 1900 through 1919. Digital Equipment Corporation moved into the complex in 1957, bought all of it in 1974 and stayed until 1998, and Maynard became known as the Mini Computer Capital of the World.

The ACS does not say who the older houses were built for. What the numbers do show is that a large share of the town's homes date from before 1940. A house of that age can have air leaks, older insulation and a heating layout designed for an earlier system. Those are reasons for a heating-load assessment before any quote, rather than matching the old unit.
## Apartments, duplexes and a rental market

The Census counts 1,369 homes in multi-unit buildings, 29.4% of the stock and 11th of the 50 towns. Owners occupy 3,439 households (77.9%), and the median value of owner-occupied homes is $459,700, 37th of 50 against $579,150 in the middle town. Two-family buildings hold 388 units and buildings of 3 or 4 units hold 223, while the 758 units in buildings of 5 or more make up 16.3% of the housing. Renters hold 977 households (22.1%), 16th-highest, which gives the rental market a real share of heating decisions in town and means many buildings have an owner who is not the occupant.

Single-family detached houses are 2,973 units (63.9%), below the 76.7% of the middle town. Rentals fall under the State Sanitary Code's heat minimums, which our heating page spells out. This is general information, not legal advice.
## Land, the refuge and the electric bill

Maynard sits on the Assabet River, 22 miles west of Boston, and borders Acton, Concord, Stow and Sudbury. Vacancy is 5.1% (237 of 4,653 units), 16th-highest of the 50. In 1942 the U.S. Army seized one-fifth of the town's land area, on the south side, for a munitions storage facility. In 2005 that land became part of the Assabet River National Wildlife Refuge, and the Assabet River Rail Trail now connects the refuge and downtown Maynard to the South Acton commuter rail station.

We cannot confirm which company supplies electricity in Maynard. Which rebate path applies depends on the utility that serves the address, and your electric bill names it. The [heat pump page](/cities/maynard/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the 2026 terms.

faq.q: Is gas the usual heating fuel in Maynard?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 63.9% of occupied homes, the 7th-highest share of the 50 towns we serve. Oil heats only 20.8%. Whether a main reaches your specific street is still a question for the gas company, and with 63.9% of homes on gas, many addresses are on one. Oil, at 917 homes, is the second fuel.

faq.q: My Maynard house is from before 1940. Do I need a heating load assessment?
faq.a: Yes. With 31.7% of homes built in 1939 or earlier, insulation, air sealing and distribution vary widely from house to house. We assess the home's heating load before quoting: oversized equipment wastes energy, and undersized equipment may struggle in January.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Maynard apartment?
faq.a: Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord, and the State Sanitary Code also sets minimum temperatures for rented units in the heating season. This is general information, not legal advice. Owners whose boiler has failed can call us at (508) 786-8755 any hour.
Our data does not confirm the utility, and your electric bill names it. Rebate eligibility follows the serving utility, so confirm at masssave.com before you order anything.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Gas heats most Maynard homes (ACS 2022), so a boiler or furnace swap often involves gas piping, venting and a permit inspection. Oil heats 917 homes (20.8%) and electricity 447, so gas is the common starting point.
body: ## Replacing gas heat in a town of older housing

Because utility gas is the leading fuel in town, many heating replacements start with a gas boiler or furnace. The gas permit has to come from a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and a new gas unit normally ends with an inspection. The town's building department can explain its local steps.
### What matters in a replacement

- The existing gas piping and its capacity for the new unit.
- Venting and the chimney or flue, which often change with more efficient equipment.
- The distribution: radiators, baseboard or ducts decide how easy the swap is.
- The heating load of the house, so the unit is the right size.
### Fuel numbers

Utility gas heats 2,822 Maynard homes (63.9%), 7th of 50, oil heats 917 (20.8%), electricity 447 (10.1%) and LP gas 179 (4.1%). Wood heats 28 homes and 23 use other fuel or coal. A like-for-like gas swap is the usual question, and the minority fuels each bring their own storage and venting details.
### Old houses

The median home is from 1963, and a large share are older. In an old house, a replacement boiler can fit differently from the one it replaces, and radiators or pipes may need attention. A cold house after a failure also needs careful restart, since pipes can be at risk.
### Multi-unit buildings

In a multi-unit building, one boiler can serve more than one household. The job may need to be planned around the days the building can be without heat, and steam or hot-water systems need careful piping and a pressure test.
### Rentals

Renters hold 977 of the 4,416 occupied homes (22.1%), 16th of 50. For a rented unit the State Sanitary Code sets a floor of 68 F during the day and 64 F overnight in the heating season, so a failed boiler is urgent for the owner.
### The minority fuels
Oil heats a minority of Maynard homes, and annual cleaning applies to those. Electricity and LP are smaller still.
### Emergencies
Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. Emergency calls are answered day and night, and the written estimate is free before any work begins.

faq.q: Can I replace a gas boiler myself?
faq.a: Not the gas work; that is for licensed trades, and the rest of the job depends on the house. A permit and inspection follow the gas connection.

faq.q: When is an old boiler worth repairing?
faq.a: If the boiler is otherwise sound and one part failed, repair makes sense. If it is old, the repairs keep coming or the heat exchanger is cracked, replacement is the better path.

faq.q: I have oil in Maynard. Can I switch to gas?
faq.a: Only if a main reaches the street, and the gas company can confirm that. Oil heats 917 Maynard homes (20.8%), 43rd of 50, so gas is the more common fuel in town, but each address differs.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Maynard has 758 units in buildings of 5 or more and 2,973 detached houses, so cooling ranges from apartment mini-splits to whole-house central air. Older buildings may lack duct space, and ductless is often the way in.
body: ## Cooling apartments, duplexes and old houses

Maynard has 2,973 detached houses and 302 attached homes, and apartments come in every size from duplexes to larger complexes. One approach does not fit all of them. Detached houses are 63.9% of units, below the 76.7% of the middle town, and multi-unit buildings hold 29.4% of homes, 11th-highest of the 50. A larger share of buildings than in a typical town are therefore not single-family houses.
### Houses with no ducts

An older gas-heated house may have a boiler with radiators or baseboard, which leaves no ducts to reuse. A ductless mini-split cools without opening walls, with one indoor head per area and a small line set to the outdoor unit.
### Apartments and shared buildings

In a small apartment building, a ductless system for each unit lets each household control its own cooling. Where tenants pay their own electric bill, that can also keep the cost with the household that uses it. Outdoor unit locations on a tight lot or a shared wall need to be planned with the owner.
### Old structures, new equipment

Maynard is 6th of 50 for homes built before 1980, with 3,300 homes (70.9%) in that group. A cooling project in such a building has to fit equipment into walls, windows and an electrical panel that were laid out long ago, which is one reason a site visit comes before the quote.
### Newer pockets and electric homes

Only 429 Maynard homes (9.2%) date from 2000 on, and 206 from 2010, 42nd of 50, so most cooling jobs involve older construction. Electricity heats 447 homes (10.1%); in those, a heat pump can cool and heat with one outdoor unit.
### Electric service
A new cooling load is also an electrical question. An old building may have limited panel capacity, so capacity should be checked before equipment is ordered.
### Detached houses with ducts
If the ducts are sound and sized for airflow, central air may suit. Ducts sized for winter heat may be too small for summer airflow.
### Sizing and humidity

An oversized air conditioner cools fast and then shuts off before it has dried the air, leaving rooms cold and clammy. Sizing the equipment from the house itself gives steadier comfort. See the [heat pump page](/cities/maynard/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) for systems that also heat.

faq.q: Can I cool a Maynard apartment without ducts?
faq.a: Yes. Each indoor head runs to an outdoor unit through a slim line set. The owner's or association's approval and the location of the outdoor unit come first.
For a single room it may be enough. With several rooms to cool, a multi-head ductless setup is quieter and leaves the windows free.

faq.q: Is a heat pump better than an air conditioner?
faq.a: A heat pump cools like an air conditioner and also heats, so it suits a space that needs both. The heat pump page covers that choice in more detail.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Gas heats 63.9% of Maynard homes, so the heat pump question is often about cooling and partial heating. The electric utility is not confirmed in our data, and the rebate path follows whichever utility serves the address.
body: ## A gas town's heat pump question

In Maynard a heat pump more often replaces an air conditioner and part of the gas heating than it replaces an oil tank. Gas heats 2,822 homes (63.9%, 7th of 50) and oil heats 917 (20.8%). Electric heat serves 447 homes (10.1%), and 179 use LP gas (4.1%). A heat pump can also heat and cool one apartment, an attic or an addition.
### Utility not confirmed

Without a confirmed utility for Maynard, we cannot say which program an address falls under. Look at the electric bill for the company's name. On the Mass Save side, the 2026 whole-home figure is $2,650 per ton with an $8,500 cap, and weatherization has to come first. Our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) carries the rest.
### Age bands against the weatherization test

Only 429 homes (9.2%) date from 2000 on, and 206 of those from 2010 (4.4%), 42nd of 50. Most owners would start with a Home Energy Assessment: 1,474 homes date from 1939 or earlier, 558 from 1940 to 1959, 1,268 from 1960 to 1979 and 924 from 1980 to 1999. Air sealing or insulation may come first in the oldest houses.
### Mixed buildings

Apartments and duplexes together make up 29.4% of the housing, 11th of the 50 towns. A ductless heat pump can serve one apartment, but the owner's approval, the outdoor unit's location and the electrical capacity come first. Detached houses, at 63.9% of units, usually have more freedom to place equipment, and the 302 attached homes (6.5%) sit somewhere between. Renters hold 977 of the 4,416 occupied homes (22.1%), so some projects will turn on a landlord's decision as much as a tenant's wish.
### Cooling in the same project

Because a heat pump also cools, it can retire a failing air conditioner in the same job. The median home here dates to 1963, 6th oldest of the 50 towns, and the heating load of such a house sets the capacity we recommend, not the size of whatever it has now.
### Heat pump plus gas boiler

A partial setup is possible: the heat pump carries most of the year and the gas boiler takes the coldest days. Gas bills and electric rates differ, so no saving is promised. Our [heating page](/cities/maynard/heating-installation-repair) covers the like-for-like replacement.

faq.q: Does my Maynard home qualify for the rebate?
faq.a: That turns on the serving utility, the equipment, the installer and the home's weatherization. Check masssave.com, because terms can change.

faq.q: Can I keep my gas boiler?
faq.a: Yes. A smaller heat pump can share the load while the boiler stays for the coldest days. We size it from the heating load of the house.

faq.q: Does a heat pump work in an old house?
faq.a: Often, once the heating load is assessed and air leaks are addressed. Maynard has 1,474 homes from 1939 or earlier, and for those the load calculation matters more than the brand.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Gas heats most Maynard homes, and gas equipment needs a yearly safety and efficiency check. With about a quarter of households renting, a tune-up before the first cold nights matters for landlords too.
body: ## Tune-ups for an old, gas-heated town

Maintenance in Maynard is mostly about gas boilers and furnaces: burner, venting, controls and the heat exchanger. A yearly check helps catch problems before a cold night does. Oil systems, the minority here, need a yearly cleaning, and 917 homes (20.8%) still depend on them. The 447 homes on electricity (10.1%) still need filter, coil and thermostat checks. Owners occupy 3,439 households (77.9%) and generally set their own service schedule. Heat pumps and cooling equipment need clean coils and filters.
### Rental properties

Almost one household in four rents (977 homes, 22.1%). A boiler that serves several apartments leaves several households cold when it fails, and the heat minimums for rentals make a September or October visit worth the trouble.
### Equipment in old buildings
In an older building, radiator valves, pipe insulation and the expansion tank all matter, along with the burner itself. With 1,474 homes from 1939 or earlier, these parts are worth a look.
### What the nameplate tells you

A boiler in any of the 3,300 homes built before 1980 (70.9%) may be original or a later replacement, and the date on its nameplate is the quickest way to tell. The 1,268 homes from 1960 to 1979 and the 558 from 1940 to 1959 sit between the oldest houses and the newer stock. A tune-up report gives each owner a condition reading, and the vacant units (237, or 5.1%) should be checked before anyone moves in.
### The smaller fuels and newer homes
LP gas heats 179 homes (4.1%), wood 28 and other fuel or coal 23. The 429 homes built since 2000 (9.2%) have newer equipment, but filters, drains and outdoor units still need their yearly care.
### Seasonal rhythm

- **September or October:** heating tune-up.
- **April or May:** cooling and mini-split check.
- **Any time:** a gas smell, soot, a new noise or short cycling is a reason to call.
### Gas safety
If you smell gas, leave the building and call the gas company or emergency services from outside. Keep your carbon monoxide alarms working.
### Owner tasks

Change filters on schedule, keep outdoor units clear, keep the area around the boiler clear and note any pressure gauge readings. Writing down the date of the last service also helps when a problem appears. For cooling, see the [cooling page](/cities/maynard/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a gas boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Yearly, ahead of the cold weather. The burner, venting and controls get a look.

faq.q: Should a landlord schedule a tune-up before winter?
faq.a: Yes. One failed boiler can leave a whole building cold, and rentals carry heat minimums, so the visit protects the landlord as well.

faq.q: What does a gas tune-up cover?
faq.a: The burner, venting, controls and heat exchanger are inspected, and combustion is tested. Gas heats 2,822 Maynard homes (63.9%), so this is the most common visit in town.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Maynard's housing runs from 1939 and earlier to 2010 and later, so air problems can differ by building. Older houses tend to leak and can hold damp, while the small group built since 2010 is generally tighter and needs ventilation.
body: ## Air quality across a century of housing

The ACS sorts Maynard's housing into bands: 558 units from 1940 to 1959, 1,268 from 1960 to 1979, 924 from 1980 to 1999 and 429 from 2000 on. The oldest band, from 1939 or earlier, is the largest single group of homes, which shapes the air story.
### Old houses

Leaky shells in old houses let in dust, pollen and damp air, though they also dilute some indoor pollutants. Old plaster, paint and insulation can matter during renovations, and dust from that kind of work can spread through a house and its ducts. A qualified specialist should test for older materials before renovation starts.
### Newer, tighter houses

Homes from 2000 on are generally tighter. That saves energy and also keeps moisture and fumes inside unless ventilation does its job. A bath fan that vents outside and a range hood help in any house, along with filters that are changed on schedule.
### Age and the work ahead

Because 3,300 Maynard homes (70.9%) predate 1980, renovation can be a good moment to think about air quality here. Opening plaster, stripping paint or pulling out old insulation can put dust into the air and the ducts, so containment and testing are part of the plan.
### Gas and oil appliances

Gas heats 2,822 Maynard homes and oil 917. Any fuel-burning appliance should vent properly, and a working carbon monoxide alarm belongs near sleeping areas. A yearly service is how problems with venting get caught.
### Apartments

Shared walls and hallways give air a path from one unit to the next in a multi-unit building, and Maynard has 1,369 such homes (29.4%). Cooking odors and smoke can ride the same path. Good ventilation and filtration help, and a landlord and tenants may need to cooperate, since a fix in one unit may depend on the building as a whole.
### Humidity
Dry winter air and damp summers both reach older plaster, wood floors and basement walls. In a damp basement, a dehumidifier handles the air, and a separate repair has to stop the water coming in.
### What we can do

- Upgrade filtration and keep filters changed.
- Add a humidifier or dehumidifier tied to the system.
- Add or fix ventilation.
- Clean ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged.
For equipment checks, see the [maintenance page](/cities/maynard/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: No, not as a routine. Ducts get cleaned when dirt, mold or damage is actually visible, and an inspection tells us whether that is the case.

faq.q: Why does my old house feel damp?
faq.a: Moisture can rise from the ground, leak from plumbing or condense where humid air meets cool walls. Finding out which comes before buying equipment.

faq.q: Does a tight newer house need a fresh-air system?
faq.a: Not always. Fans and filters are the first step. Maynard has 429 homes built since 2000 (9.2%), and for those a ventilation check can show whether more is needed.
